newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss Re to get 100 mln Sfr in deal with PartnerRe.
newsitem.headline: Swiss Re to get 100 mln Sfr in deal with PartnerRe.

text.p: Swiss Reinsurance Co said on Monday it would make a capital gain of 100 million Swiss francs through its deal to sell Paris-based Societe Anonyme Francaise de Reassurances (SAFR) to Bermuda-based PartnerRe Ltd, Swiss news agency ATS reported.
In a statement carried by ATS, Swiss Re did not give the total value of the transaction.

But PartnerRe announced in New York it would pay a total price of $950 million, made up of $800 million in cash and 6.45 million PartnerRe common shares, for the Paris-based European direct reinsurer.

PartnerRe said Swiss Re would own 79 percent of the outstanding shares of SAFR after completing the acquisition of the aggregate holdings of SAFR held by Assurances Generales de France and French insurance group Athena.
Swiss Re would then begin a cash tender offer for the remaining SAFR shares held by the public. PartnerRe said it would acquire all the SAFR shares owned by Swiss Re after that.
The statement did not make clear how much of SAFR is currently owned by Swiss Re.
Swiss Re officials in Zurich were not available for further comment on Monday, a public holiday.

But the company's statement said the deal had been agreed late in February and that the European Commission had indicated in mid-March that it had studied its compliance with European competition rules, ATS reported.
Swiss Re's statement said the transaction had yet to be approved by relevant authorities, ATS added.
